note.question: How should a community price crowdsourced electricity from electric vehicles and allocate storage and energy costs so that all consumers prefer stable omni-sharing cooperation?
note.overview: Cooperative game theory is a central solution framework: energy consumers form coalitions, the characteristic cost V(S) prices each coalition's outside option, and core allocations are constructed to make grand-coalition storage sharing stable.

models.name: Cooperative cost allocation for distributed energy sharing
models.summary: Cooperative game theory is a central solution framework: energy consumers form coalitions, the characteristic cost V(S) prices each coalition's outside option, and core allocations are constructed to make grand-coalition storage sharing stable.
objects: Coalitions S of those consumers, including the grand coalition N
Ride-sharing and private-use electric-vehicle drivers whose aggregate supply responds to the community's posted uniform price
inputs: Time-of-use grid prices and the payment rule are common knowledge
EV availability, energy, location, and type are represented by aggregate distributions; the community uses the induced energy-supply function
Every coalition can evaluate its characteristic cost V(S), including the optimal coalition structure outside S
decisions: The community chooses a uniform crowdsourcing price and quantity for EV energy
EV drivers decide whether the offered payment covers charging, spatial-mismatch, degradation, and outside-option costs
Consumers choose whether to cooperate in the grand coalition or deviate
In joint planning, the coalition selects stationary-storage capacity
The grand coalition assigns total cost to individual consumers
assumptions: The peak tariff exceeds the efficiency-adjusted off-peak energy plus amortized storage cost, making storage investment viable

EV drivers are heterogeneous by available energy and location, but battery capacity and degradation rate are homogeneous within the aggregate model; ride-sharing and private-use types may have different outside-option parameters
The crowdsourced-energy function is increasing and assumed log-concave over the viable price interval
Consumers in one community can trade stationary storage without modeling strategic interactions between neighboring communities
The cooperative game is a cost game: coalition rationality requires each coalition's allocated cost not to exceed V(S)

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: During off-peak hours, consumers and EV drivers charge storage from the grid. During the peak period, consumers first share stationary storage; the community then purchases residual energy from willing EV drivers under a uniform-price scheme and finally buys any remaining shortfall from the grid. For the cooperative-game layer, consumers either enter with installed capacities or jointly choose community capacity, then allocate realized daily cost in the storage-present game or optimized expected cost in the joint-planning game across the grand coalition. consumers compare the grand coalition's assigned costs with every subcoalition's characteristic cost a uniform EV price induces an aggregate mobile-storage supply response
